en: The *Mallikādevīpuṣpamālāsūtra*. [Posthumous title:
Kaifu Yitong Sisi, Shishi Honglu Qing, Duke of Su with an appanage of three thousand households;
granted purple robes and the posthumous rank of Sikong, with the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror).

Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, in accordance with imperial decree.
He was accompanied by two hundred and fifty great arhats,
as well as an immeasurable assembly of great bodhisattvas,
with Maitreya Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as their leaders.
Surrounded before and behind by the eight classes of beings, including the devas, nāgas,
and yakṣas such as Mālīci, Śāriputra then rose from his seat and bared his right shoulder.
Placing his right knee upon the ground and joining his palms, he addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
what dharma must sentient beings of the future, the final age, practice in order to be liberated from all calamities?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra, “Listen attentively, listen attentively!
I shall now explain this matter to you.
At that time, the assembly rejoiced and leaped for joy, and they entreated him once more.
Then the Buddha, the World-Honored One, spoke these words:
"There is a deity named Māṭali who always precedes the sun."
If one does not see the sun, or if others are unable to see the sun, one should recite this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | tadyathā | arukamas makamas adumakasi cibaramakasi andantanamasi marīciparamasi namastuṭṭe svāhā.* May it protect me from the dangers of kings and concealment.
The perils of bandits, the difficulties of travel, losing one's way in the wilderness;
the dangers of water and fire by day and by night;
the perils of rākṣasas, the ghosts of the *caṭaka* and *jinni*, and the danger of poisoned drugs.
The Buddha speaks the truth; the Dharma speaks the truth; the Sangha speaks the truth.
The devas speak the truth; the ṛṣis speak the truth. May they protect me! The mantra says:
*tadyathā | arakule arakule kili kili cile cile | amuko ’haṃ sarvabodhyabhiprāptaye svāhā*. The Buddha said: "If there is anyone who wishes to practice this rite..."
Among all dharmas, this dharma is the most supreme.
If a person wishes to make offerings to the goddess Mārīcī,
they should use gold, silver, red copper, white sandalwood, or purple sandalwood.
One should fashion an image of the goddess Mālinī.
As for the method of creating this image:
it should resemble the form of a celestial maiden (devakanyā).
The height may be one, two, three inches, or even up to one cubit (*hasta*).
Among these, the most excellent are those measuring one or two inches, which are considered superior.
Furthermore, the artisan who fashions the image must be a master of the highest skill.
One should be sent to receive the eight precepts of the fast, bathe every day,
and perform the rite wearing clean white garments.
Regarding the price of these items, one must follow the instructions of the instructor and not refuse to pay.
Once this image has been made,
if a bhikṣu wishes to travel a long distance,
he should wrap that image within a piece of his kāṣāya robe.
If an upāsaka who observes the five precepts places that image within his topknot,
he should set it aside and remove it from his body when voiding urine or excrement.
One must not perform the evacuation of feces or urine while sharing the same body space.
Next, the methods for mudrās and maṇḍalas are explained:
cross the two little fingers and the two ring fingers.
Place the right hand over the left in the palms.
Straighten both index fingers so that their tips touch.
Place each middle finger across the back of its respective index finger so that their tips meet.
With the two thumbs held upright side by side, bind the sides of the two index fingers;
move the thumbs back and forth.
This is the Mudrā of the Body Mātṛkā Dhāraṇī, following the previous body mudrā.
Next, bend the upper joints of both middle fingers;
their tips should face the thumbs with the nails hanging down and backs facing each other.
Then, bend the upper joints of both thumbs.
The head is directed toward the palm;
this is the Seal of the Crown of the Head.
If a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī...
Wrap the aforementioned image within a *kāṣāya* robe;
if it is for a layperson, place the image within their topknot,
and then form this "topknot mudrā" (*uṣṇīṣa-mudrā*) to seal the image.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times while walking on the road.
Following the previous hand gesture, simply extend the tips of the two index fingers by about two finger-widths;
this is the protection-of-the-body mudrā, used for the method of protecting the body.
Press the tip of the left thumb against the first joint of the ring finger;
clench the remaining four fingers into a fist—this is the mudrā of joy.
If one recites the mantra while performing this mudrā when facing a king or a minister, [the purpose will be accomplished].
Then the person before him, with joy, bends his left arm and draws [the other] forward;
he forms a fist by grasping with the four fingers starting from the index finger,
and presses the thumb down upon the nail of the index finger.
Next, open the palms and make a hollow in the center.
Extend the right hand with the palm facing upward,
directed toward the joints of the left hand.
Rub the palms together until they reach the openings of the fingers;
then, cover the finger openings with the right palm while performing this mentally.
The palm of the left hand is the heart of Māricī;
the palm of the right hand is the body of Māricī.
Within the center of the palm of the left hand...
Wherever my body may be, let the Mālinī deity conceal my body;
let Mālinī remain upon the crown of my head to protect my body.
This is the seal (mudrā) of Mālinī.
One who recites the mantra repeatedly within the mouth will immediately obtain great efficacy.
The practitioner must not eat cooked rice;
they may consume only barley, milk, curd, ghee, vegetables, and the like.
If you cannot endure [the hardship], you may beg for food for yourself,
but you must not eat the food belonging to the Sangha.
When you have completed one hundred thousand repetitions in this manner, you will obtain the spiritual efficacy.
Within a clean and purified maṇḍala, one should install an image of Mañjuśrī.
The practitioner should bathe every day;
if they do not bathe, they must wash their hands and rinse their mouth before entering the maṇḍala.
Forming the bodily mudrā, summon Mārīcī.
Having established her, make various offerings.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, or one thousand and eight times, every day.
In this manner, continue until one hundred thousand recitations are completed.
Thereafter, prepare the ground in a suitable location;
having removed all undesirable things such as tree roots, shards, gravel, hair, and bones.
Firmly build it upon the ground and make it level.
The day for constructing the altar is the fifteenth day of the twelfth month;
construct it using the five colors.
In the center, place a pedestal for Mālatī.
Upon the seat, paint a flower throne together with her image.
Then, station the messenger facing east.
The one named Bhadrasiriya is stationed in the north;
his messenger is named Keśinī.
To the south, one should establish the messenger named Mārīcī;
thereafter, the mantra-practitioner summons her and installs her there.
Having made various offerings with eight plates of incense, flowers, and food, and sixteen lamps,
the mantra-practitioner sits at the western gate facing east.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
After completing various offerings, then dismiss [the deity].
There is another method for the days of solar and lunar eclipses.
One who performs this rite for constructing the altar will obtain great efficacy.
If a person intends to travel far to the east or west while on the road,
they should first construct a water altar.
Having summoned Mārīcī and established her there,
take non-glutinous rice and flowers mixed with clarified butter;
recite the mantra once for each offering, burning them until one thousand and eight offerings have been completed while simultaneously chanting the mantra.
Whoever proceeds to whatever destination they desire shall obtain great efficacy.
Furthermore, there is another method: for seven days, one should daily construct a water mandala and summon Mañjushrī to be installed therein.
Furthermore, having placed a fire hearth and kindled a fire of *śāla* wood,
one should recite the mantra over one hundred and eight grains of non-glutinous rice and black sesame seeds while they are being burned in these embers, and continue to chant the mantra.
Recite this one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
Once this ritual has been completed for seven days,
those who previously fled in all directions will return to the presence of the king and his ministers.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to engage in debate,
one should follow the previous ritual by burning one hundred and eight segments of pear branches—
one chi each— while reciting the mantra for seven days.
One who performs this rite shall become a great master of treatises.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times over ghee while it is being burned in fire as per the previous rite,
no birds, beasts, venomous insects, or other creatures shall be able to cause harm.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person wishes to see Mārīcī,
they should follow the previous rite by kindling a fire with fuel from the *śirīṣa* tree and take twenty-one pieces of celestial wood (*devadāru*).
Anoint it with ghee, honey, and curd;
burn it while reciting mantras day after day.
For food, consume only these three things: non-glutinous rice, milk, and ghee.
One must not consume other food.
During these seven days, one should provide various offerings that increase twofold each day.
While performing this rite in this manner for seven days:
On the seventh day, at midday, Mārīcī manifests her body.
Entering the maṇḍala, she asks the practitioner:
"What dharma do you seek?"
At that time, the practitioner answered as he pleased.
When Māṭali gave his consent for him to depart, he immediately knew that the sign had been obtained;
all the devas were likewise filled with joy.
Furthermore, there is another method: during the seven days, perform this three times each day.
Burn the three substances—fennel, white calamus, and white mustard seeds—with fire while reciting the mantra;
then, upon approaching the person toward whom one is directed, that person will become joyful.
Furthermore, if one wishes to approach an official,
one should follow the previous method by burning white mustard seeds in fire,
reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times for each of the three periods of the day.
During these seven days, one may consume only three things— polished rice, milk, and curd—
and must not eat anything else.
When the seven days have concluded and one approaches the official, the latter will be delighted.
Furthermore, according to the previous method,
one shall burn one hundred and eight *āmalaka* leaves with fire while reciting the mantra over them.
By doing so for seven days, one will cure all diseases caused by spirits and achieve efficacy.
Furthermore, according to the previous method:
take large barley grains and grind them well, but do not reduce them to powder;
mix them with honey and form one hundred and eight pellets, each the size of a plum.
During the seven days, the practitioner shall abstain from food entirely on the first day;
for the remaining six days, one may eat as desired.
Every day, one shall burn a ball of barley while reciting the mantra.
Form the mudrā of supreme joy (*parama-pramuditā-mudrā*) and, having thus completely burned one hundred and eight pellets,
extinguish the fire with water. Then, inhale the smoke from it and fumigate both palms,
reciting the mantra twenty-one times.
The vow says: "May my hands be able to bring about all manner of efficacious attainments in all dharmas.
Thus, one attains all efficacious powers, and those before whom one acts are filled with joy.
Furthermore, regarding the ritual for those suffering from feverish illnesses:
Take fresh green grass and hold it to the mouth;
recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Rub it upon the patient fifty-four times, and both the patient and the practitioner will be cured.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should recite the mantra once every day;
three times for the great protection of the body,
and three times for the great establishment of the boundary.
If one recites the mantra five times, one will obtain whatever person one desires at will.
If one recites the mantra six times to establish a boundary,
one shall have no fear whatsoever when entering a cemetery at night.
Furthermore, if one intends to travel a long distance,
one should first burn incense of *kunduruka* seven times in a private room while reciting the mantra.
When setting out on the journey, the practitioner should recite the mantra repeatedly.
On the road, dangers from bandits and demons shall all be unable to approach.
Furthermore, according to the previous method,
on the eighth day of the waxing moon, one should perform this in a pure chamber.
Take fine incense, flowers, and a small amount of non-glutinous rice;
burn them one thousand and eight times over a fire.
The practitioner of the rite shall not eat for one day.
One who performs this rite wearing clean and pure garments shall be respected, honored, and provided with offerings by others.
Furthermore, there is another method: take cow dung before it has fallen to the ground.
Receive [the water] in a vessel and do not let it fall elsewhere;
immediately mix it with water to create a water-maṇḍala.
Place an image of the Buddha or a relic of the Buddha at the center of the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, take the milk of a mother cow and her calf along with that of a yellow cow to make ghee.
Place it in a golden bowl and stir it with the ring finger of the right hand.
Regarding the ghee and the mantra:
if fire should emerge from atop the ghee,
one should know that one will attain great intelligence, such that one can recite a thousand verses with a single recitation.
If fire does not emerge and there is only smoke and warmth,
one knows that it can be made bright;
if neither smoke nor warmth is obtained, [it cannot].
Prostrate yourself on the ground with your mouth positioned beside the vessel of ghee.
Using the ring finger of your right hand as a spoon, consume the ghee;
you will immediately attain a small measure of intelligence.
Furthermore, there is another method: outside the eastern gate of the city, prepare the ground well and construct a four-cubit altar.
Take five unbaked bricks.
In the center, place one [image] with four faces, one on each side;
furthermore, fill four water jars with water and plug their openings with willow branches.
Place it upon the bricks at the four corners.
Then, take red sandalwood and grind it in water;
immediately sprinkle that water upon the altar.
Offer red flowers upon the altar. Furthermore,
take four pieces of *huln-ji* and place them individually beside each of the four water jars.
Furthermore, wrap five-colored threads around the four sides of the altar.
Outside the four sides of the altar,
arrange various kinds of flowers, incense, food, and drink.
Paṇḍita, together with the various spirits,
spreads seats of green grass at the four gates of the altar.
The mantra-practitioner, wearing fine, clean robes, sits cross-legged upon the green grass.
He summons Mārīcī and her various messengers and establishes them there,
making manifold offerings.
The mantra-practitioner holds green grass in his hand and recites the mantra.
Rub the grass from one's head toward the feet one hundred and eight times.
The mantra-practitioner forms the *mālīcī-kāyāmudrā* with his hands;
within this mudrā, he holds the fresh green grass and places it upon his own crown.
He dispatches one disciple to take four water jars from the altar and pour them one by one over the head of the mantra-reciter. Once this is completed,
the mantra-reciter puts on clean, fine garments and performs the protection-seal (*rakṣā-mudrā*).
Having finished reciting the Buddha’s name, prostrating to the Buddha,
and paying homage to Mārīcī, take three substances:
nāgakesara flowers, camphor, and ghee-blended incense.
During the seven days, the mantra-practitioner shall consume only rice and cow’s milk porridge,
and must not eat any other substances.
Day by day, he shall recite the mantra over the three aforementioned medicinal substances one hundred and eight times.
Up until the seventh day,
if one places that medicine upon the crown of the head, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, the throat, or the forehead,
the efficacy will be realized.
This statement does not inquire into the distinct function of the dharma.
Furthermore, the dharma depends on what precedes it.
If a person suffers from hemorrhoids, [the following applies].
Take black thread to fashion a mantra-cord.
Have the patient lie upon a bed with the head toward the east and the feet toward the west,
and bind the patient’s waist with the cord.
Furthermore, if one ties a rope to the legs of the bed and recites the mantra twenty-one times, hemorrhoids will be immediately cured.
As for the method of treatment for those suffering from neck ailments:
Following the above, one should only change the previous practice of binding it around the waist;
the difference is that it is bound upon the neck.
Furthermore, there is another method: take the mud from both banks of a river.
One should fashion one hundred images of ghosts;
among them, the king of ghosts is named Vināyaka.
This king of ghosts has a head shaped like that of an elephant.
The remaining ghosts each have heads shaped like various birds and beasts,
while their bodies, hands, and feet are entirely made in human form;
they should be fashioned at a size of four or eight finger-widths in height or length.
Take red sandalwood and grind it with water;
using that water, mix it with clay to construct an altar upon the ground.
Using soil of five colors,
construct seats upon the altar:
one seat at the center and two seats facing north.
There are two seats facing south and two seats facing east.
Place an image of the King of Ghosts upon the central seat;
on the remaining six seats, distribute and place images of ninety-nine ghosts in total.
Offer various kinds of incense, flowers, seven lit butter lamps, food, drink, and so forth; furthermore,
take guggulu incense and mix it with clarified butter.
The fire is used for making offerings.
The mantra-reciter sits at the western gate facing east and recites the Mārīcī mantra seven times.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times over various colored threads.
Then, take the images of the various spirits from the three sides of the altar and gather them together to place in one location beside the central image of the King of Spirits.
Having bound all those ghost-images together with thread of seven colors,
take one hundred and eight lumps of calf dung.
Burn each [piece] with fire while reciting the mantra.
At the time of burning each ball, recite the mantra once.
First, chant "Svāhā" (pronounced *sba-ha*) and say, "Bind all ghosts."
Then, chant "Svāhā" (pronounced with the *praśliṣṭa* and *āyatta* vowels) one hundred and eight times, until all the pellets have been exhausted.
In another location, dig into the earth to a depth reaching the waist and make a hole.
Place the images of the various ghosts who were bound by him into the holes,
and make offerings to those ghosts with various incenses, flowers, and diverse foods and drinks.
Thereafter, seal the openings from above with the aforementioned materials.
If one firmly builds [the boundary] so that it is level and restored,
those spirits will never be able to emerge. If,
at the time when the karmic illness of that mantra-practitioner approaches death, [this is done...]
Mentally intending to liberate that ghost, the ghost shall be released.
If one performs this rite, one will immediately obtain the great efficacy of Mārīcī.
All mantra-rites will be efficacious.
Furthermore, there is a method: throughout one's life, eating only rice-milk porridge every day and reciting the mantra repeatedly, one will attain great intelligence.
Among the four castes, the Brahmins hold him in great affection;
if he burns ghee, curd, or milk,
the Kṣatriyas hold him in affection.
If fire burns barley or curdled milk,
the Vaiśyas will feel affection;
if fire burns sesame dregs, [the same applies].
Śūdras hold him in affection.

Furthermore, according to the Dharma, if a person afflicted by a human or ghostly illness is completely unable to speak, one should recite the mantra over water twenty-one times and sprinkle it upon them; they will immediately speak.
Furthermore, if one suffers from a ghost-induced illness characterized by the mouth being closed and unable to speak,
chant the mantra twenty-one times over a corner of a *kāṣāya* robe and strike [the patient] with it;
they will immediately speak.
Furthermore, there is a method: take ashes in the hand, recite the mantra over them seven times, and scatter them in the four directions to establish a boundary.
Another method is to fashion ten mud pellets the size of marbles and throw them toward each of the ten directions to establish a great boundary.
Furthermore, if a woman experiences difficult labor,
one should recite the mantra over black sesame oil seven times;
by rubbing it upon her navel, she will give birth easily.
Furthermore, there is another method: when one gains the upper hand in debate with others, and is consequently hated, resented, or addressed with harsh words by them;
or when one engages in conflict with others.
When one is falsely accused by another and brought before the authorities to be interrogated regarding the truth or falsehood of the offense,
take white calamus and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times.
Tie it to the right arm.
Then, with the left hand, form the mudrā of joy and recite the mantra over it.
One will immediately attain the principle of great victory.
If one recites the mantra frequently, various efficacious results will be obtained.
Furthermore, if a person has been stung by a venomous insect,
the mantra-master should take thread of five colors and fashion a consecrated cord with twenty-one knots.
Having finished tying it upon his own right arm,
he went toward the person who had bitten him and took a willow branch, over which he recited the mantra.
If one repeatedly rubs that person with the hand, they will immediately recover.
If a person has been bitten by a venomous snake and is on the verge of death,
the mantra-master takes water in his own cupped hands.
Rinse the mouth seven times while reciting the mantra;
by sprinkling this water upon the patient twenty-one times, the illness will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, if a person develops malignant sores on the body:
If one applies mud mixed with earth over the sore twenty-one times while reciting the mantra, it will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, if a domestic animal contracts an epidemic,
one should kindle a fire of *gokṣura* wood at the exact center of the city.
By burning cow’s milk with fire and reciting the mantra, the ailment will be cured immediately.
This rite should be performed at night;
on the following day at noon, one should again burn the fire of *śirīṣa* wood.
Take white mustard seed oil and mix it with white mustard seeds.
If one burns [the mixture] over one thousand and eight repetitions while reciting the mantra, the ailment will be cured.
Furthermore, another method is to take one thousand and eight pieces of *kruddha* wood—this wood resembles the bodhi tree—and burn each piece individually while reciting the mantra once for each.
All the kumbhāṇḍas, yakṣas, and other spirits will be entirely delighted.
If one recites [the mantra] one thousand and eight times over a small amount of winter melon while it is being burned by fire,
all the piśācas will likewise be entirely delighted.
If one takes one thousand and eight pieces of wood from trees upon a cemetery,
mixes them with sesame seeds, burns them while reciting a mantra one thousand and eight times,
all great and malevolent spirits and ghosts will be delighted.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one takes one thousand and eight segments of a Bodhi tree branch,
anoints each one with clarified butter, burns them one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings will rejoice and hold one in loving remembrance.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person suffers from epilepsy,
the mantra-practitioner should take all five grains, mix them together,
scoop them up with his hands, and recite the mantra over them while burning them in fire one thousand and eight times.
The ghosts and spirits will rejoice, and one will immediately be cured of illness.
If one takes安息香 (guggulu), grinds it into pills, coats them with clarified butter,
and burns them over fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, [the same result will follow].
Maheśvara and all the deities surrounding him were filled with joy.
If one constructs a maṇḍala according to the aforementioned rites and performs various offerings, [the result will be attained].
Place an image of the Buddha or a relic of the Buddha at the center of the maṇḍala.
Take three thousand eight pieces of khadira wood—this is another name for the *kaṭhilla* tree—and [prepare them].
Anoint each section with ghee, curd, and honey,
and burn them one by one in the fire while reciting the mantra once for each.
In this manner, complete all three thousand eight sections.
One who performs this rite shall extinguish the four grave offenses and the five heinous crimes and obtain its efficacy.
If the practitioner completes the water mandala according to the preceding method, from the eighth day to the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight.
If one takes one thousand and eight pieces of purple gingerwood daily,
anoints them with ghee, burns them in a fire while reciting mantras,
Māricī will immediately enter the ritual circle and fulfill all one's wishes.
At that time, the practitioner shall see the body of Mārīcī with their own eyes and obtain great efficacy.
If one does not eat for a single day and performs this rite with various offerings,
one will obtain the great efficacy of Mārīcī.
Furthermore, if one wishes to obtain wealth and riches,
during the two days from the fourteenth to the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight,
one should take three portions each day of black sesame, non-glutinous rice, and the flowers of non-glutinous rice.
By burning [the substance] and reciting the mantra, one immediately obtains wealth.
Furthermore, if one wishes to bind Māra,
one should take branches of the *kaṭuka* tree every day for seven days.
One name is Bodhivṛkṣa (Bodhi Tree).
If one takes one thousand and eight pieces and burns each one in a lamp filled with white mustard oil, [the following occurs].
One will immediately be bound.
If a mantra-practitioner or a layperson performs this rite of incantation and the authorities become aware of it and seize them, [they shall suffer the consequences].
When one is bound by shackles and fetters,
if this mantra is recited repeatedly, the bonds will never hold.
If people are at enmity with one another, take the dregs of sesame oil and mix them with the husks of non-glutinous rice.
If one performs the fire-oblation one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra,
the person who was angry will immediately become joyful.
If one takes black sesame seeds and performs the fire-oblation one thousand and eight times, [the same result follows].
The person before will feel affection and joy.
Furthermore, if one wishes to obtain wealth,
one should take the stems of pomegranate grass every day for seven days.
If one takes six fingers' length of [the substance] in one thousand and eight segments,
burns each one in fire while reciting the mantra,
one will immediately obtain wealth and property.
Furthermore, if one wishes to seek a cherished object from another person,
one should take white calamus and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
By tying it upon one's own arm, whatever one begs for shall be obtained.
Furthermore, according to another method, for twenty-one days, at the three sessions of each day,
take *guggulu* incense and pound it into one thousand and eight pills.
Then, coat them with clarified butter, curdled milk, and honey.
Regarding each instance of burning with fire and reciting mantras:
if one approaches the king and his officials, those people before him will feel joy, love, and affection.
If one wishes to become a leader or administrator, [one should do so].
During the seven days, at the three sessions each day,
one should take various kinds of fragrant incense and pound them into one thousand and eight pills.
Each pill should be smeared with ghee and burned in the fire while reciting the mantra.
One will immediately attain the fundamental principles.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a practitioner bathes and enters the maṇḍala to perform various offerings such as a water altar,
they should summon Mañjuśrī and establish him there.
Thus, perform this rite one hundred thousand times.
When the practice is completed, then say the words for binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*) with the mouth, rather than forming mudrās with the hands.
Whatever the practitioner desires shall be accomplished.
All difficult matters can be easily accomplished;
however, this applies except for the matter of destroying another's ritual performance (*karmasthāna*).
At that time, Mālikī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Blessed One, I have another method which I now wish to explain:
take fine red sandalwood three finger-widths wide and three inches long;
on one side of that wood, carve the form of Māricī."
She is fashioned as a female deity.
On the left and right sides of her image,
two Mālikas are carved as attendants.
She is also fashioned in female form.
Furthermore, a separate cover made of red sandalwood is used to cover it.
Once this image has been completed:
Desiring to travel a long distance,
he intended not to part with this image from his person;
he concealed it so that no one would know of its existence.
Recite the mantra repeatedly every day.
If you have a specific aspiration and wish to construct a water mandala,
place an image at the center of the mandala.
He summoned Māṭṛceṭa and established him there,
making various kinds of offerings.
Furthermore, he took one hundred and eight lotus flowers to offer as worship.
As for the method of making offerings:
take each lotus flower one by one with the hand, consecrate it with mantras, and use it for offering.
Furthermore, perform the fire sacrifice (*homa*) one thousand and eight times with black sesame and non-glutinous rice, reciting the mantra throughout.

One should understand that regarding the statement "to obtain various kinds of efficacious results," all the aforementioned dharmas must first be performed using water mandalas and other such offerings before one can attain their efficacy.
Thus did Māliṃji conclude his exposition of this dharma.
Together with the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, they prostrated to the Buddha and withdrew.
*Tadyathā*: *aragule aragule kiliṭi ti sarvagalahi pi-pa-sapū upatuseḍe sarva-iti-syu upadralapi lekha lekha mo mā amukaṃ yasya svāhā*. According to one manuscript, it says: "Svāhā."
The method for creating an image of a deva:
the image has two hands;
the left hand bends the arm upward and extends it horizontally.
Place the fist before the left breast;
within the fist, hold a whisk (cāmara) in the manner held by a Dharma-preacher while seated upon a high throne.
Within the whisks, one should fashion the shape of the ten-thousand-character script of the Western Regions,
similar to the characters upon the chest of a Buddha image;
within each of the four curves of the characters, one should further fashion the shape of a sun.
Attach each of these, placing four sun-marks upon them.
On the whisk, fashion a flame shape.
Extend the arm and fingers of the right hand, letting them hang down.
Regarding the method for making images:
there is no difference in the manner of painting them.
The height of the image may be one inch, two inches, or even up to one cubit.

*Tadyathā | arakuli arakuli kṛtiṣṭha sarvaga rākṣasi saputrabhāryā saparivārā sarvetuṣṇībhūtā rakṣa rakṣa mama amukaṃ svāhā.* This mantra is intended for the purpose of subduing; hereafter, this mantra shall be used to bind thieves.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī spoke this mantra:
"Homage to the one with a thousand-fold turning head!
Namaḥ mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya | tadyathā | hili tiṣṭha tadbhakara pūtu kṣamadhara svāhā. Furthermore, if while traveling on a road one encounters bandits...
If one recites the mantra over the thumb of the right hand and firmly grasps the fingers,
one will encounter no difficulties even when meeting bandits.
If one recites the mantra over the sleeves or the lapel of one's garment, [the same protection is obtained].
Recite the mantra seven times while quickly passing over [the area].
This is the mantra for removing sleep: *Tadyathā | idimi ti ji ti bika na śandi padāci svāhā*. If a person is very drowsy while sitting, [they should recite this].
If one recites this with a sincere mind before the Buddha seven times, even minor ailments will vanish.
The mantra of Vaiśravaṇa is as follows:
*Namo vaiśravaṇāya mahārājāya dhanadāya svāhā*. If one recites this over pure oil seven times, or fourteen times, [it shall be effective].
Use it to anoint the place where one sleeps;
one will obtain wealth and goods according to one’s wishes.
This is the mantra for subduing all thieves: *puruṇa puruṇa jūruha jūruha svāhā*. There is also another mantra for binding thieves.
*Kaṭa kaṭa saṃkaṭa*. I now perform *kaṭa*, never for the sake of releasing *kaṭa*. Furthermore, if one is beset by bandits, one should burn incense and recite this mantra;
if there are any doubts, one should also invoke my name.
If you do not know [the incantation], you should simply face the thief and recite the mantra over them.
The thief will then bind themselves and confess to the stolen goods.
Once this has been obtained, release them; this is a great and proven efficacy.
The Mallikādevī Mālya Sūtra (The Discourse on Queen Mallikā and the Flower Garland)
